reviews.one_line_contribution: It turns "does experience memory need a query" into a manipulated variable by wrapping ALFWorld in randomly-coded protocols that add hidden preconditions, multiplying the number of distinct procedures from 6 to 288, and claims the retrieval residual over a cached compiled prompt appears only above a threshold procedure count and is erased by a factorized (6 procedures + 48 protocol rows) table — so the determinant is the size of the smallest compiled form, not the raw procedure count.
reviews.closest_prior_work: VERIFIED: Enrich-Retrieve-Rank (arXiv:2608.22695, 2026-08-24, confirmed via s2cli paper; S2 and HF both returned it). It already asserts the proposal's mechanism — in-context routing over a registry degrades as the candidate set grows, and an offline-enriched retrieve-then-rank pipeline restores accuracy at lower cost as the registry scales. The proposal's differentiators are real but narrow: task success on one environment instead of Match@1, a compiled and a factorized table as controls, and the count varied within a single environment rather than compared across registries. It does not threaten the factorization claim, which I found nowhere. Second verified threat: Demystifying Agent Skills: Why They Work — Until They Don't (arXiv:2608.14036, 2026-08-14, verified), a controlled contrastive study concluding that skills help by acting as procedural anchors that stabilize execution rather than by supplying missing knowledge, and naming retrieval as a bottleneck mode; that is the same content-vs-routing decomposition the oracle arm here is built to make, on a broader task set but with no count manipulation. Also verified and adjacent: SGR-Bench 2605.22219, Mem2ActBench 2601.19935, WALL-E 2.0 2504.15785 — all cited accurately, none manipulates procedure count or compares against a compiled set. Not individually verified (relied on in the related-work paragraph but not checked here): Toolshed 2410.14594, ScaleMCP 2505.06416, Graph RAG-Tool Fusion 2502.07223.
reviews.strongest_objection: The proposal's premise is contradicted by the binding measurement it is built on, which makes the headline threshold unidentifiable. The abstract asserts that "a 400-token cached prompt listing all six [procedures] is a complete substitute for retrieval" and the hypothesis asserts "ALFWorld spans P = 6 and shows no residual." Measurement C on this node says the opposite: instr_all, the ~400-token type-agnostic six-procedure prompt, is 20.1 net BELOW k=3 retrieval, and even the best static arm (static3, three type-conditioned exemplars) leaves k3 − static3 = +17.2 net [+11.9, +22.4]. The R = 1 all-P compiled arm in this design is essentially instr_all plus a protocol line, so P2 ("at R in {1,4}, retrieval minus all-P compiled <= +8 net") is very likely already falsified at the bottom rung by roughly 20 net, before any procedure-count effect exists. With a large residual at R = 1 there is no threshold in R to find: the ladder would measure the growth of a residual that is already above the confirmatory margin, and the P3-vs-P2 contrast that carries the paper dissolves. A second, independent defect, flagged by the entailment check and confirmed on reading: the R = 4 length placebo is the R = 4 content padded with 264 procedures from protocols not in force, i.e. a 288-row code-keyed table with one matching row — exactly the routing load of the R = 48 all-P prompt. If P3 holds because routing among 288 code-keyed rows fails, the same mechanism falsifies P4; P3 and P4 cannot both pass, so the "it is routing, not length" defense is unavailable as designed. Third, the manipulation is not really "procedure count": the protocol codes are deliberately random strings with no inferable content, so the all-P arm measures exact-match string lookup in a 10k-token cached prompt (a needle-retrieval property), not the semantic discriminability that governs procedure selection in a real bank. A threshold found here would not transfer to the deployment question of how many procedures a prompt can hold.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Re-anchor every prediction to the measured +17.2 residual over static3 rather than to an assumed null at P = 6: state P2 as a level ("retrieval minus best static at R = 1 equals the measured +17.2 ± 5") and make the claim about the CHANGE in residual with R, with the change, not the level, carrying a bootstrap CI; if the residual is already +17 at R = 1, say what a threshold would mean. (2) Match representation across arms: the compiled and oracle arms carry procedure text while retrieval carries full trajectories, and Measurement C already prices that gap at 17-20 net, so add exemplar-form static arms — an oracle-routed three-exemplar arm from the correct (type, protocol) cell (the true routing-free upper bound) and an all-P exemplar arm where it fits — otherwise "compiled loses to retrieval" is the known representation gap, not routing. (3) Rebuild the placebo to pad with non-table filler at matched token count while holding code-keyed distractor rows at 24; as written it changes both length and distractor count. (4) Make the keys semantic rather than random strings (or run both), so the result speaks to procedure count and not to literal-string lookup, and report protocol-row identification accuracy separately from task success so routing failure is observed, not inferred. (5) Raise the manipulation check to the +14 confirmatory margin or add seeds (P1 sits exactly on the ±8 floor), predict the 8B-vs-32B residual difference at a fixed R with a CI instead of comparing threshold locations on a three-point grid (P7), and state a multiplicity rule for P6's four-cell "at any R" test.
reviews.missing_baseline: An oracle-routed exemplar arm — three fixed expert trajectories from the correct (type, protocol) cell, cached, no query — and its all-P counterpart. The brief binds every retrieval claim to the BEST static alternative, and on this node that is static3 (exemplars), not a procedure sentence; every static arm here is procedure text or a single oracle procedure, so no arm isolates routing from the exemplar-vs-procedure representation gap Measurement C already measured at 17-20 net. Also missing: a retrieval arm at R = 48 restricted to the correct protocol's items (retrieval with perfect keying), which would separate "the query carries the binding" from "the retriever ranks well".
reviews.preprint_collision: No verified collision. All nine queries ran through channel (a), the s2cli literature command (S2 + HF; both channels reported ok on every call); WebSearch is unavailable in this session and WebFetch is blocked, so channel (b) answered nothing. (1) 'number of procedures in context routing residual retrieval versus compiled prompt agent' --recent -> Enrich-Retrieve-Rank 2608.22695, Scalable Prompt Routing 2603.19415, Token Reduction Is Not Cost Reduction 2607.12161; nothing manipulating procedure count on one environment. (2) 'scaling number of skills in prompt versus retrieval task success threshold agent procedural memory' -> Demystifying Agent Skills 2608.14036, When Single-Agent with Skills Replace Multi-Agent Systems and When They Fail 2601.04748 (skill-library scaling limits), SkillEvolBench 2605.24117, SkillRet 2605.05726, Skill Retrieval Augmentation 2604.24594, Managing Procedural Memory 2606.23127 — the closest cluster; none varies the count as a controlled knob against a compiled table. (3) 'all tools in prompt versus tool retrieval as library size grows task success crossover' --recent -> CaSKG 2608.25500, HYSET 2607.25718, SkillRet 2605.05726, ToolRet 2503.01763; recall-oriented, no all-tools-in-prompt control. (4) closest named methods verified with s2cli paper: 2608.22695, 2605.22219, 2601.19935, 2504.15785, 2608.14036 all exist with the described content; Toolshed 2410.14594, ScaleMCP 2505.06416 and Graph RAG-Tool Fusion 2502.07223 were NOT individually verified here. (5) home-vocabulary query with no agent/memory words: 'in-context example selection versus fixed demonstration set as number of task variants grows' -> 2405.00200, 2506.04579, 2308.00675, 2305.14907; classic ICL selection, none on a count threshold. (6) 'when is retrieval necessary versus putting everything in the cached context long context agent controlled study' --recent -> EvoMemBench 2605.18421 (long-context baselines beat memory systems), LongMemEval-V2 2605.12493 (AgentRunbook-C compiled vs AgentRunbook-R retrieval — a compiled-vs-retrieved pair the proposal does not cite and should), Harness the Memory 2608.15008. (7) 'compressibility of a knowledge set determines whether retrieval beats a static compiled instruction table' -> empty for the claim (only KV-cache and model-compression papers), which is the strongest support for the factorization half of the hypothesis. (8) 'ALFWorld variant with unstated action preconditions agents must learn from experience' --recent -> 2605.05413, WALL-E 2.0 2504.15785 only; nobody plants protocol-keyed preconditions. (9) 'synthetic environment variants with injected hidden rules to control how much knowledge an agent must retrieve' --recent -> 2607.19616, 2606.23271, 2603.02091, 2510.13913; empty for the claim. Judging the proposal's own check: it is unusually good — four query classes, recency-restricted, IDs given, and it correctly names ERR and SGR-Bench as nearest work; my searches reproduce it. Two gaps: it misses the skill-library scaling cluster (2608.14036, 2601.04748, 2605.05726, 2606.23127), where the 'routing over many skills degrades' claim is closest to being scooped, and it misses LongMemEval-V2's compiled-runbook vs retrieval pair. Novelty is scored on what I verified: the count-manipulation-plus-factorization design is unclaimed, but the routing-collapse claim it rests on is already ERR's.
